summary:
plan.md is written. Along Pike Place (east, +x) the building climbs from a low green-posted North Arcade shed (y 19) through a 2-storey block to a 3-storey white-brick Main Arcade over a red/white-awninged stall shed, all on a grey stone Down Under that drops west to the bay with window tiers by ground level.
It peaks in a flat-roofed corner block at Pike Street (z 280..311) carrying the red-neon PUBLIC MARKET CENTER sign (red glass over glowstone, east face, y 48..69), a two-faced red-ringed clock, MEET THE PRODUCER and the fish ice beds: the market's postcard view.
Not tested: I didn't run the roof tool's dry-run on any roof, and I placed the sign letters and the clock by hand on paper, so their fit still needs a render. All block ids pass the toolkit's block check and exist in 1.21.1. White quartz-brick Main Arcade over a stone Down Under base, with a green-post stall arcade along the east street face and the open North Arcade shed to the north. The hero is the south-east corner: red neon PUBLIC MARKET CENTER sign, round neon clock, MEET THE PRODUCER board and the fish ice beds. Dusk glow comes from froglight behind the panes, hung lanterns in every bay and glowstone behind the red glass letters.

The render shows the west tiers and the white upper block.

summary:
North shell, shed frame, arcade floor: North shell built in parts/shell-north.mjs: A (footing, polished andesite floor y19, west wall x29 with 2x2 window openings, 33 posts with head beam y25), B1 (footing, floor y20, west wall x29, posts x40 with beam y27), B2 (walls x22/x33 and end walls to y31, upper floor y26, shopfront band and window rows left air), S (footings, floors y20/y22, posts x40 with beams at floor+5), and slab ramps at z132, z188, z279.
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt; my part places 12819 blocks with no refused writes except B2's street floor y20 (336 cells the south shell already owns) and no off-palette blocks. Zoomed renders show the green posts, head beams and window openings reading as the arcade.
polish: Roof R-A, R-B1, R-S and R-B2 are not built here; the head beam y25 sits where the roof's eave course will go, so the roof part may conflict with it.

Ground: build.mjs fills ground with base.mjs's placeholder groundY before any part runs, so cells above the real GROUND map can keep stray cobble. My footings use a local GROUND table (overwriting ground), but nothing carves ground above the floor. The real map belongs in base.mjs.
B2 street floor y20 is refused as written, because the south shell's DU already owns those cells. Confirm DU ends at the street floor.

Small orphans from post_bay's end brackets at z0 and z132 (dark_oak_stairs at 33,24,0 and planks at 33,25,132; similar at the B1 and S run ends). They touch the build on one face only, so the check reports them as orphans; trimming the end runs fixes this.

Facade openings are air as the plan requires: A west windows (y21..22), B2 shopfront band (y21..23 on x33) and B2 window rows (y28..30). The B2 window rhythm uses (184-z) mod 6 and may not match the facade's bay grid exactly.
No roof.json yet, so the roof was skipped by build.mjs. Nothing checked against the roof.

waste.cost: three zoom renders and reading the images
waste.tool: mcd zoom --sweep over a mass's faces, with a per-face check that openings are air.

companions.task: Give the real per-cell ground heights for the plot so the footings and the street-floor steps come from measured ground, not a linear placeholder.
Make the brackets and the B2/S beam ends meet the posts and walls cleanly, so the end runs are not orphans.
Confirm the head beams at y25 and y27 sit at the eave course, so the R-A and R-B1 roof bases don't collide with them.

summary:
Roofs and chimneys: Roofs and chimneys built in parts/roofs.mjs: R-C via roof.json (keep for two stacks); R-A, R-B1, R-B2 and R-S by roof() calls; R-D parapet y43, stepped quartz gable of D to y45, shed slab flashing at x34, three brick stacks.
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt: roofs part shows 0 refused and 0 off-palette; check reports 0 floating; fit is OK.
Open: roof reads as one tone (palette has one roof field block), gable ends carry no overhang by design, the R-C slope is 91 long with no dormer or chimney break.
polish: Roof reads as one tone: palette.json's roofs list has only deepslate_tiles (plus slab/stairs), so the roof tool's ROOF_SINGLE_MATERIAL warning stands. A second field block needs a palette decision.
R-C is one 91-cell slope with no break (ROOF_BIG_PLANE). The two chimneys are dummy stacks from stack(), not the roof tool's chimneys option, so the tool does not count them as breaks.
Gable ends of R-A, R-B1, R-C and R-B2 have overhang 0 on the north and south sides (ROOF_NO_OVERHANG). This is by design: the ends butt into neighbouring masses.
R-S flashing is a single slab course at x34 above the high edge. It was not visually checked against the upper wall.
The stepped gable of D is quartz_bricks at z 280 for x 14..33, computed from R-C's pitch, not checked from the front.
Render was only checked at small size (front-left tile); the roof line and stacks were not inspected close up.
plan.md checklist ticked for part 3 and a note added there. elements.md has no checkbox column, so its items 3, 20 and 21 were not marked.

waste.what: Roof tool warnings were fixed by trial and error: each pass changed one material key and rebuilt (palette fascia, soffit, ridge, mix), with about four rebuilds to get off-palette and ridge warnings clear.
waste.cost: about 5 build and report cycles, each a full make.sh run
waste.tool: roof --spec should print the palette role each roof key (verge, fascia, soffit, ridge, eave) draws from, and warn when a key falls back to a non-palette default such as spruce.

waste.what: The roof spec holds one footprint and one eave, so five roofs at different heights needed hand-written roof() calls in build() beside roof.json.
waste.cost: four roof() calls with duplicated material and overhang options
waste.tool: roof.json should accept a list of rects with their own y, pitch, ridge and overhang, so a multi-roof part is one spec.

waste.what: Stack and shed-flashing coordinates were worked out by hand from the plan table: each stack's ridge and eave, and the flashing y per z band.
waste.cost: about 6 coordinate computations and one loop over z
waste.tool: A vocab helper for a shed high-edge flashing course (shed_flashing(g, {x, z0, z1, y})) and roof.json could take the stack list from the plan.

waste.what: No visible check of the roof line: the tiles were too small to read the stacks or flashing, so I could not confirm them by eye.
waste.cost: one render plus reads of small tiles
waste.tool: mcd zoom at the roof line (for example zoom --at 34,28,170) would show the flashing and stack without a full-site render.

companions.task: Pick the second field tone for the dark slate roof, check the R-C slope break, and confirm the verge and fascia choices against the palette.
Look at the three stacks' bands and caps from the street and set the chimney masonry for the R-C pair and the R-B2 stack.
Set the quartz-brick stepped gable of D and the flashing course where the shed meets the upper wall, so they line up with the facade's string courses.

summary: Facades: windows, doors, trim, awnings, lamps: ["parts/facades.mjs builds the facade layer on C, B2, D, the street arcade and the North Arcade west wall: glazed bays (dark oak mullion), shop doors and shopfront panes at x33, Down Under windows and four doors, red/white awnings, cornices, string course, quoins, hanging lanterns and trade signs.", "make.sh produces a whole build.nbt: the facades line shows 2656 placed, no REFUSED writes, no off-palette blocks. `mcd fit` reports OK. plan.md checklist ticked for 4 facades.", "Not verifiable yet: the lamps, signs and awnings need the North shell's posts and head beams (part 2 placed 0 in this run), so they place only after merge. Froglight glow was dropped (refused into shell air)."]
polish: Froglight glow is absent: the vocab's glow cell lies in shell interior air, which runParts refuses, so no window has a glow.
Window sills and lintels are not placed: they would fall outside the footprint at the plot edge; the windows are flush glass with a dark oak mullion.
Lamps (hang_lamp), trade signs (stall_sign) and awnings depend on the North shell's head beams and posts; the North shell placed 0 blocks in this run, so they are unverified until the merge.
Shop door lintels at x34 show as orphans (single contact with the wall); the shop decorator's display, stock and wood settings for sockets.json were not set here.
Down Under doors (x0 z300, x7 z236, x14 z200, z311 x10) have no slab ramp; the approach standard is unmet.
D south-face cornice and the A-arcade lanterns were not built. Pilasters go through pier_bay and are placed only where the air allows.
B2 west glazing (x21, z161..188) floats in this run because the wall at x21 is not built by the shells yet; it should attach after merge. Check after merge.
elements.md has no tick column; items 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 19 and the lamp part of 6 are built here, pending the North shell.

waste.what: Transcribed the 45x7 GROUND table by hand from the brief into a local array, then derived the Down Under window grid cell by cell.
waste.cost: ~45 rows typed once, plus grid arithmetic for each wall run and level
waste.tool: A ground map file or groundY(x,z) that reads the brief's GROUND table (plan.md should carry the values; base.mjs groundY is a placeholder).

waste.what: window_bay and du_window put sills and lintels one cell proud. On the west and south faces at the plot edge those cells fall at x=-1, x=20 or z=312, outside the footprint, and the B2 west windows floated. I rewrote glazing locally (bayGlass, duGlass, southGlass) to avoid them.
waste.cost: 3 failed build runs (out-of-bounds and footprint throws) plus a rewrite of the glazing calls
waste.tool: A window helper with an 'in-plane' mode (no proud sill/lintel) for wall planes at the plot edge, and a window_bay muntin that is glass or framed rather than an open trapdoor (open trapdoors float over the shell's interior air and fail fit).

waste.what: Froglight glow behind every window: the shell leaves interior air as placed, so runParts refused the ochre_froglight writes (223 refusals in the first run). Dropped the glow rather than place it.
waste.cost: One full rebuild and a manual decision
waste.tool: A runParts option or shell convention that leaves a named glow cell open (or lets facades write into shell-interior air that no later part needs).

waste.what: Checked the facades by hand against the plan's coordinates (bay grids 160+6k, 190+6k, 224+6k, 252+6k; D windows skipped at the clock cells). No tool lists per-face bay starts.
waste.cost: About 20 coordinate lists computed by hand
waste.tool: A bay-grid helper that emits the window starts for a face from a plan row (e.g. faceBays(plane, z0, z1, grid)).

companions.task: Set the window glass with true connections and the dark oak mullions and sill frames, and fit the froglight glow behind each pane where the shell leaves a cell open.
Shop door pairs and the lowered Down Under doors (hinges, transoms), plus the cornices and string courses as joined stair lips.
Hang the chain lanterns under the head beams once the North shell has placed them, and check that each lantern is lit and visible at dusk.
Letter the hanging trade signs (FRESH PRODUCE, FLOWERS, FISH, HONEY, BAKERY, CRAFTS) and check them from the street.
Ramp the Down Under doors at grade with the half-step slab approach so the way in meets the accessibility standard.

summary:
Corner landmarks: neon sign, clocks, board, fish market: Built parts/landmarks.mjs: PUBLIC MARKET CENTER neon sign (neon_sign at x37, y43, z279..310), east and south market clocks (radius 3, neon ring), MEET THE PRODUCER board (producer_board at x41), and the fish ice bed (ice_bed x35..40, z296..309, y24). make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; the landmarks line has 2679 placed, no off-palette blocks, no orphans, and check/fit are clean.
Renders read: the sign reads PUBLIC / MARKET / CENTER left to right from the east, and the clock reads as a clock (two hands, ring) and the ice bed reads as fish on ice.
Open: MEET THE PRODUCER letters are not placed (the board is 4 rows, too short for block letters, and banner letters would hang at x42, off-plot); 8 neon-ring glowstone cells fall in the D wall and are refused by the shell, so the east ring reads red without glow there.
polish: MEET THE PRODUCER letters not placed: the board is 4 rows (y 42..45); block letters need 5 rows and banner letters hang at x 42 (off-plot). Needs a taller board or a letter plane in the parapet (plan.md Notes).
PUBLIC MARKET banner text under the east clock not placed (no free row in the reserved box; optional in the spec).
8 neon-ring glowstone cells behind the east clock (x 40, y 35..40, z 305..308) are refused by the shell's D wall, so that part of the ring reads red without glow. The south clock glow is placed.
Elements 15-18 are marked built in elements.md; 17 is marked built with its letters missing.

waste.what: Checking each landmark by hand: zooming four separate views (sign, east clock, south clock, fish bed) and reading the PNGs one by one to confirm the letters and faces.
waste.cost: 4 zoom renders plus reads, about 2 minutes
waste.tool: A `mcd landmarks-check` (or card --layout landmark) that renders each named landmark in one sheet with its expected text and face, and flags the reading order automatically.

waste.what: Finding the 8 refused glow cells and the orphan glowstone by trial: the make.sh refusal list was the only signal, and the orphan showed up only in `check` after the build.
waste.cost: 2 rebuilds and one check run
waste.tool: A pre-flight in runParts or market_clock that lists the cells a helper wants to fill with force writes, and which of them sit in an earlier part's walls, before they are written.

waste.what: Working out clock and sign centres and leg positions from the plan by hand (east centre z 305, south centre x 36, neon z0+2 step 8).
waste.cost: A few coordinate calculations
waste.tool: The SIGN, CLOCK and PRODUCER_BOARD constants in vocab/base.mjs could carry a `centre` and `legs` field so parts pass the object through instead of re-deriving it.

waste.what: Checking whether the producer board could carry its lettering: reading plaquePlan's block-letter and banner rules to find out the 4-row board fails both.
waste.cost: One source read of brush-sign.mjs
waste.tool: `plaque --dry-run` that reports which styles fit a band and why none does, so the plan can change the band height before the letters are attempted.

companions.task: Put MEET THE PRODUCER on the board (a 4-row band, so banner letters must hang on a taller board or a plaque in the parapet), and the PUBLIC MARKET banner strip under the east clock.
Open the 8 glow pockets in the D wall at x 40 behind the east clock ring (y 35..40, z 305..308) in the shell, before the landmarks part, so the neon ring has its glow.
Wire and light the neon-sign redstone lamps and the clock ring from one switch so the sign and clocks come on together at dusk.

summary:

polish: Flower buckets (flower_bucket) not placed: no free post base at the North Arcade (lanes and tables fill x30..32) and the S post base cells are counter or slab cells.
Standing lanterns on posts not placed: the post tops sit under the head beams, so there is no free top. Lanterns on the counters would sit in goods cells, so I left them to facades' hang_lamp.
honey kind replaced by flowers (honeycomb_block is off palette); the palette has no honey block, so either add it to palette.json or accept the swap.

The shop-decorator and redstone-engineer duties in the brief (sockets.json, display, stock, fascia) do not apply to this part's coordinates: there is no sockets.json in this directory, so `$MCD sockets check` was not run.
elements.md has no tick boxes, so I did not mark elements items; items 4 (stalls) and 14 (craft-stall tables) are built here, minus the flower buckets and lanterns above.

companions.task: Heap the produce counters with the right mix of melons, pumpkins, hay bales and apples, and decide which stalls read as flowers or fish from the street.

companions.role: stair joiner / carpenter for the counter and table frames
